transcript:
Header: 2026-08-30 10:00 AM UTC | Duration: ~55m | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (CTO), Liam (Head of ML), Sofia (Platform)

Summary (auto): Demo of Redwood migration path from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together. Showed API parity examples, console mapping, and Redwood Optimize recommendations. Action items and next steps captured.

00:00:03 Alex Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, and Priya is our solutions engineer. 
00:00:10 Maya Chen: Hi, thanks, we appreciate it, excited to see the migration path.
00:00:15 Priya Shah: quick agenda — we'll cover API parity, model mapping, console demo, then Optimize suggestions and finally deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). happy to stop for Qs.
00:00:30 Liam O'Neill: sounds good. our immediate goal is to reduce token spend by 20% and keep latency at sub-200ms for chat endpoints. we currently use OpenAI for chat and Together for some RAG tasks.
00:00:48 Alex Martinez: got it. and do you have any compliance constraints — SSO, SOC2, data residency?
00:00:55 Sofia Ruiz: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, and KMS integration. also prefer VPC peering for production.
00:01:05 Priya Shah: great — Redwood supports SOC2, SAML/SSO, and customer-managed KMS for Private deployments. For hosted we offer KMS-backed encryption with audit logs.
00:01:20 Alex Martinez: ok we'll show where those settings live in the console in a bit.
00:01:28 Priya Shah: first, API parity. Many of you asked how to translate existing OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls to Redwood. so i'll share a live parity mapping sheet and show examples.
00:01:45 00:01:50 Priya Shah: (screen) here's a typical OpenAI chat completions call — model, messages, temperature, max_tokens. On Redwood we have a /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints, param names are similar but we also expose batch_id, route hints for smart routing.
00:02:10 Liam O'Neill: so the payload is identical? any required fields we should watch for?
00:02:15 Priya Shah: mostly identical. one difference: Redwood separates model_variant and runtime_profile — so you can pin quantized variants or low-latency variants. also streaming is compatible; we support SSE and websockets, similar to what you have with OpenAI streaming.
00:02:32 Alex Martinez: another gotcha — token accounting differs a bit depending on tokenizer. our parity sheet lists per-model token multipliers to help estimate cost.
00:02:45 Maya Chen: can we keep the same stopping tokens and tool calling? we rely on tool-calling heavily.
00:02:52 Priya Shah: yes — function/tool calling maps to Redwood's structured output + tool schema. there's a small mapping for Anthropic-style 'instructions' -> Redwood messages but we included examples.
00:03:06 00:03:15 Priya Shah: for Together, the main change is sequence-length defaults — Together tends to accept longer context by default; Redwood allows you to set seq_len and we have auto-caching for prefixes to reduce compute.
00:03:30 Liam O'Neill: what about embeddings? we use OpenAI embeddings for semantic search right now.
00:03:36 Priya Shah: Redwood embeddings endpoint is /v1/embeddings, identical semantics: input array, model param. We also support batched embeddings and async batching for high throughput. we can show a code snippet.
00:03:52 Priya Shah: (screen) here's a sample curl migrating from OpenAI to Redwood. note the header change to Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_KEY> and the model map — e.g., text-embedding-3-small -> redwood-embed-s1.
00:04:10 Maya Chen: lovely. is the latency comparable? we see 80-120ms for embeddings now.
00:04:18 Priya Shah: depends on model and deployment. Hosted Redwood often gets similar latency; for aggressive SLAs we recommend Dedicated GPU pools. also Optimize can suggest quantized model variants that bring cost down while keeping latency within your SLO.
00:04:35 00:04:50 Priya Shah: demo: Console. (screen) Top left is API keys, below is routes and per-route SLOs. You can pin a model version per route; here's where you'd enable VPC-only access for a route in Private.
00:05:05 Sofia Ruiz: where do we configure KMS?
00:05:09 Priya Shah: in Settings -> Security -> Key management. For Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS via IAM roles and HSM options. For hosted, we support customer-managed keys via Bring-Your-Own-KMS.
00:05:22 Alex Martinez: also audit logs export to your S3 or SIEM via delivery hooks.
00:05:30 Maya Chen: good. now on to Optimize features — can you explain batching recommendations?
00:05:40 Priya Shah: sure. Redwood Optimize analyzes your traffic patterns and suggests batch sizes and prefilling to maximize GPU throughput with minimal latency impact. it simulates token arrival and recommends a batching policy (e.g., 8 concurrent requests or 512 token window).
00:06:00 Priya Shah: it also suggests kv-cache policies so repeated prefixes get cached and don't recompute. that drives down per-token cost for chat-heavy workloads.
00:06:12 Liam O'Neill: any risk to response quality when quantizing?
00:06:16 Priya Shah: small regression possible; Optimize includes evaluation harnesses — you can run your prompt set and get quality delta estimates per quant profile. we recommend a human-in-the-loop check for critical flows.
00:06:30 00:06:45 Alex Martinez: typical migration path customers take: start hosted with a small pilot, run parity+benchmarks for your key prompts, validate quality with Optimize, then decide Dedicated or Private if you need capacity or compliance.
00:06:58 Maya Chen: timeline-wise we want to be in pilot within 2-3 weeks.
00:07:02 Alex Martinez: doable. we'll include a default pilot pack with 100k tokens, benchmark scripts, and a parity spreadsheet.
00:07:12 00:07:25 Liam O'Neill: question on fallback policies — if a Dedicated node is full, can we fallback to hosted or another region?
00:07:30 Priya Shah: yes — smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants and different capacity tiers. you can define cost/latency-based routing.
00:07:42 Sofia Ruiz: how about network peering for Private? we prefer VPC peering and strict IP allow lists.
00:07:49 Priya Shah: supported. Private deployment offers VPC peering, private endpoints, and private control plane options. we also offer an on-prem appliance for air-gapped needs.
00:08:05 00:08:20 Maya Chen: any limitations on GPU types for Dedicated? we use A10G internally, is that supported?
00:08:27 Alex Martinez: we support a range — A100, A10G, H100 on some configs. Priya can follow up with a hardware list for your region.
00:08:40 Priya Shah: (screen) now switching to parity mapping doc — here's row examples: OpenAI "gpt-4o" -> Redwood "redwood-gpt4o-v1" with recommended runtime_profile "low-latency". Anthropic "claude-2" -> Redwood "redwood-claude-compat". Together mappings include throughput variants.
00:09:06 00:09:20 Liam O'Neill: are there any code changes beyond model names and minor param renames?
00:09:25 Priya Shah: mainly header, model field, and optional route hints. We provide SDK wrappers that allow a drop-in replacement for most node/python libs. We'll share a repo with examples.
00:09:40 Maya Chen: pricing: will you share estimated cost delta for our typical traffic?
00:09:45 Alex Martinez: yes — we'll run the parity cost model using your sample payloads. that's part of the pilot analysis.
00:09:55 00:10:10 Sofia Ruiz: security — we need SOC2 Type II evidence and penetration test reports.
00:10:15 Alex Martinez: we will share our SOC2 report and pen test certs; for Private we can add additional contractual SLAs.
00:10:26 00:10:40 Priya Shah: quick note on telemetry: you can turn on redaction for PII before logs leave your VPC. also token-level cost dashboards live in Console -> Analytics.
00:10:55 00:11:05 Liam O'Neill: ok, let's talk benchmarks. we need to run three workloads: chat latency, embeddings throughput, and a RAG pipeline using Together-format long contexts.
00:11:15 Priya Shah: great — we'll provide benchmark harnesses. For RAG, Redwood's prefix caching and async batching usually shows 20-40% cost savings.
00:11:30 Maya Chen: any gotchas migrating stored embeddings? we have millions in postgres.
00:11:36 Priya Shah: embeddings are binary-compatible in terms of vector outputs per model mapping. we recommend re-indexing with the mapped model for parity, but you can also run A/B to compare.
00:11:50 00:12:05 Alex Martinez: we should also talk about rate limits and concurrency model — Redwood exposes per-key rate limits and per-route throttling. you can request increases for pilot.
00:12:15 Sofia Ruiz: good. one more — data residency: EU-only data flows for GDPR.
00:12:21 Priya Shah: we have region-specific deployments, including EU data planes and private deployments with EU-only networking.
00:12:30 00:12:50 Maya Chen: okay, this has been useful. can we see a short live run of an OpenAI -> Redwood request and streaming response?
00:12:55 Priya Shah: yes — demo. (screen) hitting demo endpoint, stream starts... 00:13:20 Priya Shah: (streaming) "...and that's the first para, finishing up now, apologies for the audio glitch" — (laughter) sorry transcription.
00:13:35 Liam O'Neill: looks identical in shape. how do you surface model drops for rollouts?
00:13:42 Alex Martinez: Console -> Deployments. you can do canary or A/B, set traffic splits, and rollback automatically if latency or quality regressions exceed thresholds.
00:13:58 00:14:10 Maya Chen: ok next steps recap?
00:14:12 Alex Martinez: we'll send: parity spreadsheet, pilot pricing, benchmark harness, SOC2 docs, and example SDK repo. we'll aim to get the POC kickoff on 2026-09-07.
00:14:30 Sofia Ruiz: thanks. we'll send sample workloads this week.
00:14:36 Priya Shah: action items noted. any final questions?
00:14:42 Liam O'Neill: one more on cost controls — tagging requests to attribute cost per team?
00:14:48 Alex Martinez: supported — request metadata and tags let you slice cost per-team or per-route.
00:14:55 00:15:05 Maya Chen: great. thanks everyone.
00:15:10 Alex Martinez: thanks, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts.

(Transcript ends — remaining time used for quick internal sync off-mic)
